    10  /-!
    11  # Homology of short complexes
    12  
    13  In this file, we shall define the homology of short complexes `S`, i.e. diagrams
    14  `f : X₁ ⟶ X₂` and `g : X₂ ⟶ X₃` such that `f ≫ g = 0`. We shall say that
    15  `[S.HasHomology]` when there exists `h : S.HomologyData`. A homology data
    16  for `S` consists of compatible left/right homology data `left` and `right`. The
    17  left homology data `left` involves an object `left.H` that is a cokernel of the canonical
    18  map `S.X₁ ⟶ K` where `K` is a kernel of `g`. On the other hand, the dual notion `right.H`
    19  is a kernel of the canonical morphism `Q ⟶ S.X₃` when `Q` is a cokernel of `f`.
    20  The compatibility that is required involves an isomorphism `left.H ≅ right.H` which
    21  makes a certain pentagon commute. When such a homology data exists, `S.homology`
    22  shall be defined as `h.left.H` for a chosen `h : S.HomologyData`.
    23  
    24  This definition requires very little assumption on the category (only the existence
    25  of zero morphisms). We shall prove that in abelian categories, all short complexes
    26  have homology data.
    27  
    28  Note: This definition arose by the end of the Liquid Tensor Experiment which
    29  contained a structure `has_homology` which is quite similar to `S.HomologyData`.
    30  After the category `ShortComplex C` was introduced by J. Riou, A. Topaz suggested
    31  such a structure could be used as a basis for the *definition* of homology.
    32  
    33  -/

    36

    40

    42

    46  namespace ShortComplex
    47  
    48  /-- A homology data for a short complex consists of two compatible left and
    49  right homology data -/
    50  structure HomologyData where
    51    /-- a left homology data -/
    52    left : S.LeftHomologyData
    53    /-- a right homology data -/
